# Accessibility Requirements Quality Checklist: SPEC 002

**Purpose**: Formal pre-`/speckit-tasks` gate — validate that the bounded
accessibility requirements in the SPEC 002 spec (keyboard operability, accessible
names/roles, landmarks, focus management, AA contrast, color-independence) are
complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before tasks are derived.
**Created**: 2026-09-08
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Evaluation history**:
- **2026-09-11 (pass 1, pre-implementation review)**: assessed every CHK against the current spec.md, plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md and tasks.md. **15 satisfied, 4 gaps (0 HIGH, 0 MEDIUM, 4 LOW)**. No functional scope was changed; no new tasks were required. Gate: **ABIERTA (open) — sin HIGH/MEDIUM pendientes.**

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is the enumerated list in FR-054 (formulario de acceso, las siete entradas de navegación, la acción de cerrar sesión) exhaustive against every interactive control this spec introduces (e.g., a password show/hide control, the section-error actions)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-054]
  - PASS: current FR-054 text explicitly lists "el control de mostrar/ocultar contraseña si existe" and "las acciones de la vista de error de sección" alongside the login form, the 7 nav entries and logout — both controls flagged by this item were added in the 2026-09-08 clarification session and are now exhaustive.

- [ ] CHK002 Are the required accessible name and role stated per enumerated control, or only required in aggregate? [Completeness, Spec §FR-054, §SC-022]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): FR-054 and SC-022 state the accessible-name/role requirement in aggregate ("DEBEN exponer un nombre y un rol accesibles" / "100% … con … nombre y rol accesibles"), not broken down per control in the spec text. `contracts/visual-system.md` §2 I3 and §3 (per-component sections) do give per-control detail (e.g., the password toggle carries its own `aria-label`) — but that granularity lives in the design contract, not the spec.

- [x] CHK003 Does the spec identify a programmatic landmark for each of the four named zones — navegación, identidad de producto, contexto de sesión, contenido — including "contexto de sesión", which has no standard landmark role? [Completeness, Spec §FR-054]
  - PASS: FR-054 explicitly anticipates this exact gap ("regiones identificables mediante landmarks **o una región con nombre accesible equivalente para el contexto de sesión**"); `contracts/navigation-and-routes.md` §4 assigns concrete landmarks (`banner`, `navigation`, `main`) plus a named `aria-label="Sesión"` region for session context.

- [ ] CHK004 Is a document/interface language requirement (Spanish, programmatically exposed) stated for accessibility, or only as a UI-copy requirement? [Gap, Spec §FR-049]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): FR-049 only mandates that "la interfaz visible" stay in Spanish — it does not mandate a programmatic `lang="es"` document attribute for assistive technology. Non-blocking because FR-054's closing sentence explicitly puts full screen-reader conformance (which is what would consume `lang`) out of scope; `plan.md`'s Project Structure notes `index.html`'s `lang` is unchanged from SPEC 001 (already Spanish).

- [x] CHK005 Are focus-management requirements defined for the failed-login case, not only for "iniciar y cerrar sesión"? [Coverage, Gap; Spec §FR-054]
  - PASS (resolved in current spec): same finding as `checklists/auth-session.md` CHK007 — FR-054 now explicitly covers the failure case.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "el foco DEBE moverse de forma razonable al iniciar y al cerrar sesión" defined with a specific target element for each transition, or left to interpretation? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-054]
  - PASS: FR-054 names a specific target per transition — Inicio's module header on login, the access form on logout, the error message (or the form) on failure.

- [x] CHK007 Is SC-022's "el foco se reubica de forma coherente" expressed as an observable expectation (named destination elements)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-022]
  - PASS: SC-022 names the same three concrete destinations as FR-054, verbatim.

- [x] CHK008 Is the boundary between "nombres/roles accesibles" (in scope) and "lectores de pantalla / orden de foco exhaustivo" (out of scope) precise enough to avoid a contradiction? [Clarity, Spec §FR-054, §Assumptions]
  - PASS: FR-054's closing sentence and the Assumptions accessibility bullet state the same boundary consistently, with no overlap between the in-scope and out-of-scope lists.

- [x] CHK009 Does "operabilidad completa por teclado" define the expected interaction (activation keys, no keyboard trap, visible focus throughout), or only that elements are reachable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-054]
  - PASS: FR-054 itself specifies "alcanzables, activables y sin trampa de foco"; visible focus is specified separately by FR-041 (foco de teclado state) and the `--focus-ring` contract in `contracts/visual-system.md` §1.3 — together the three properties (reachable, activatable, visibly focused, no trap) are all covered.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK010 Is FR-040's "contraste suficiente" reconciled with SC-016's explicit WCAG 2.1 AA ratios (4.5:1 / 3:1) so there is a single contrast bar for this spec? [Consistency, Spec §FR-040, §SC-016]
  - PASS: same finding as `checklists/visual-ux.md` CHK014 — FR-040 explicitly states the same threshold as SC-016.

- [x] CHK011 Are the interaction states in FR-041 (including "foco de teclado") consistent with the keyboard-focus-visible expectation in FR-054 and SC-022? [Consistency, Spec §FR-041, §FR-054, §SC-022]
  - PASS: same finding as `checklists/visual-ux.md` CHK015 — unified by the single state matrix in `contracts/visual-system.md` §4.

- [x] CHK012 Is the "un elemento deshabilitado NO DEBE aparentar estar disponible" requirement (FR-041) consistent with the accessible-name/role and keyboard-operability requirements for the same controls? [Consistency, Spec §FR-041, §FR-054]
  - PASS: `contracts/visual-system.md` §4 specifies `aria-disabled="true"` for the disabled state, which communicates unavailability without stripping the control's accessible name or role — no conflict with FR-054's name/role requirement.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK013 Are the color-carrying UI states that must remain distinguishable without color enumerated exhaustively (semantic states + active module), or could other color-only signals exist unaddressed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-039, §SC-015]
  - PASS: same finding as `checklists/visual-ux.md` CHK022 — FR-039 is a blanket rule and SC-015 is exhaustive over the complete set of color-carrying signals this spec actually defines; no other such signal exists in scope.

- [x] CHK014 Is the "un icono no puede mostrarse" scenario (FR-024) covered for its accessibility consequence — the entry still exposes an accessible name via its visible text? [Coverage, Spec §FR-024, §FR-054]
  - PASS: `contracts/navigation-and-routes.md` §3 N2 confirms the icon is `aria-hidden` and the visible text label carries the accessible name regardless of whether the icon renders — the consequence FR-024 requires is structurally guaranteed.

- [ ] CHK015 Are reduced-motion / animation-related accessibility expectations addressed or explicitly declared out of scope? [Coverage, Gap]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): no artifact mentions `prefers-reduced-motion`, and it isn't declared out of scope either. The practical risk is low because FR-030(b) already caps every animation at ≤150ms with no looping — a duration well under common motion-sensitivity thresholds — but the media query itself is neither required nor explicitly excluded.

- [x] CHK016 Are keyboard/focus expectations defined for the section-error view and the six "No disponible" views, or are those assumed to contain no interactive elements? [Coverage, Gap; Spec §FR-044]
  - PASS: the six "No disponible" views are explicitly forbidden from containing any interactive element (`contracts/visual-system.md` §3.6 — no `button`/`input`/`form`/`select`/`role="button"`), so no keyboard requirement applies there by design; the section-error view's actions **are** explicitly included in FR-054's keyboard-operable set.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK017 Does SC-016 define which "componentes de interfaz esenciales" are in scope for the AA contrast check across the login and the seven areas? [Clarity, Spec §SC-016, §FR-040]
  - PASS: same finding as `checklists/visual-ux.md` CHK005 — FR-040 enumerates the pairs, tabulated with ratios in `contracts/visual-system.md` §1.4.

- [x] CHK018 Is SC-015's "simulación de percepción sin color" specified (method and which views) so the "100 %" result is reproducible? [Measurability, Spec §SC-015]
  - PASS: same finding as `checklists/success-criteria.md` CHK010 — `quickstart.md` E13.2 specifies the exact tool/method (Chrome DevTools Achromatopsia emulation).

- [ ] CHK019 Does SC-022 state how "se puede alcanzar y activar solo con teclado" is judged across browsers, given SPEC 001 documented WebKit keyboard-focus differences? [Measurability, Spec §SC-022]
  - GAP (LOW, non-blocking): SC-022 states verification happens "en los tres navegadores de escritorio soportados" and `tests/e2e/keyboard-a11y.spec.ts` (tasks.md T073) runs explicitly across Chromium/Firefox/WebKit — but neither the spec nor the plan calls out a specific accommodation for the WebKit keyboard-focus quirks SPEC 001 is said to have documented. Cross-browser execution would surface a WebKit-specific failure if one exists, but there is no documented special-case handling for it here.
